newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Police say Belgian bin bag murderer killed three.
newsitem.headline: Police say Belgian bin bag murderer killed three.

text.p: Belgian police investigating the crimes of an unidentified serial killer who terrorised the city of Mons by leaving a trail of bin bags containing the severed limbs of several women, have pieced together three corpses.
"I can confirm there were three victims," Dominique Hautier, spokesman for the Mons public prosecutor's office said by telephone on Monday.
Police originally believed that the 30-odd neatly severed body parts -- including arms, legs, hands, feet, a torso and a head -- belonged to up to six women.

Investigators have already identified one of the victims as 21-year-old Nathalie Godart, who frequented the fringes of society in the southern Belgian city that is also home to the military headquarters of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
However, Hautier refused to confirm a report by Belgian RTBF television that the other two bodies had also been identified.
"I can say nothing about that at all," he said, adding that formal identification could take up to two more weeks.

Police began finding the gruesome bin bags in late March, and have since been trying to identify the victims and build a psychological profile of the killer who is believed to be either a local or at least to have a thorough geographic and historical knowledge of the city.

Many of the bin bags have been found in places with names carrying deep symbolism, such as the Hate River, Worry Street and St Symphorien Street -- the name of a third century French saint who was beheaded and whose bones rest in a local church.
At one stage police arrested a local man for the killing of Godart, but were forced to release him due to lack of evidence.
No more body bags have been found since late April.
